title: Fragile Beauty Conducts Heat Well
text:
Fragile Beauty Conducts Heat Well. This COPCO FLIGHT ENAMEL ON STEEL TEA KETTLE (5197724; 2.4-Quart, White) is beautiful, with a graceful modern design. It’s enameled both inside (black) and outside (white). It conducts heat well—on my ceramic-top stove, it took only a few minutes to heat half a kettle of water. It has an urgent, piercing (but NOT annoying) steam whistle that tells you the water is boiling.

Unfortunately, it is fragile. Mine was dropped, and the black handle snapped off cleanly where it joined the silver top of the kettle. The kettle is now useless. (I could glue the handle back on, but I don’t trust even superglue to hold the entire weight of a tea kettle filled with 2.4 quarts of boiling water.)

This model has one other negative feature—the maximum fill line is marked with a sticker on the front of the tea kettle, but not with anything you can easily see when you’re filling the kettle. Even if you set the kettle down (so that the water surface is level), It’s difficult to follow the instruction to “ensure water level is below Max Fill line or at least ¼” below the bottom of the inside spout opening”.
